properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 18 at 3:13PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue
rising, reaching Moderate flood stage tonight due to strong onshore
flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy
rainfall expected in the Astor area.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
occurring and moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog & Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 2.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 PM EST Wednesday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.6 feet Sunday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 315 AM EST.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 18 at 4:27PM PST until November 18 at 6:45PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban areas and small streams flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Alameda and Contra Costa Counties...

* WHEN...Until 645 PM PST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 427 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in
the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- The main rain band is exiting the East Bay. Flooding will
diminish over the next few hours with additional rounds of
scattered showers likely across the region tonight into tomorrow.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Oakland, Fremont, Hayward, Concord, Richmond, Antioch, Livermore,
San Ramon, Pleasanton, Union City, Walnut Creek, Pittsburg,
Dublin, Danville, Martinez, Oakley, Pleasant Hill and San Pablo.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 4:58PM PST until November 18 at 7:30PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Plaskett burn area in...
South Central Monterey County in central California...

* Until 730 PM PST.

* At 458 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the Plaskett Burn Area. Between 1.5 and 2.5
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to
0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and
Prewitt Creeks. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Plaskett Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Plaskett Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile marker 11 including
Los Burros Road.
properties.instruction:
Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, and roads is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain. Impacted
areas include locations along Los Burros Road, areas near Plaskett
Creek Campground and structures along the Alder, Plaskett, and
Prewitt Creeks.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 18 at 8:07PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage.
Additional heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours will continue to
produce river rises, approaching record flood level late this week or
this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 17.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Wednesday was 17.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.4 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued November 18 at 8:01PM EST until November 18 at 9:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Jupiter Inlet to Deerfield Beach FL out 20
NM...

* Until 900 PM EST.

* At 801 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Palm Beach, moving northwest at 20
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Riviera Beach, Ocean Ridge, Palm Beach, Hypoluxo, South Palm Beach,
Manalapan, Briny Breezes, North Palm Beach, and Palm Beach Shores.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.
